content:
Eden: quick follow-up from the RFC: we should expose a lightweight "fallback signal" so runtime can declare why a higher-precision profile wasn't used (e.g. missing kernels, mem pressure, tenant lock).
Kofi: +1. suggested codes: NO_KERNEL, MEM_PRESSURE, TENANT_POLICY, FP_MISMATCH. Runtime emits X-precision-fallback: NO_KERNEL for traceability.
Lena: ops implications: when fallback occurs, we should mark the response with metadata so downstream evals can separate natural model drift vs fallback-caused drift. propose header: X-precision-effective: orig=...;effective=...;fallback=CODE.
Eden: also add a short JSON-friendly log line to join on: "precision_event": "orig:vendor/fp8/x -> resolved:redwood/int8/y;fallback:NO_KERNEL". keep it compact.
Kofi: on policy: default behavior = try exact profile else fallback to compatible same-architecture profile, but block cross-architecture (fp8->int4) unless owner-approved.
Lena: runbook snippet: if fallback rate > 1% for 5m -> alert oncall and open incident with model-owner; also auto-enable a shadow run with original profile for diagnostics.
ops-bot: ticket created: QUANT-FALLBACK-407 assigned to eng-ml.
Eden: action items: 1) add fallback codes enum to runtime logs (Kofi) 2) expose headers for tracing (Lena) 3) update onboarding lint to require fallback safe-list (Eden).
Kofi: I'll send a tiny PR for the enums today.
Lena: will draft the header spec and console display for fallback counts.
Eden: thanks, let's keep fallback explicit so we don't silently mask quality issues. :thumbsup:
